brief.recommendation: Active change window CHG-7452 (BIZ-3) has policy consult_owner for marketplace_listing_reindex, so Catalog Engineering must approve any interruption (I3). audit.report: The marketplace_listing_reindex job, which claimed a freeze exemption, became an idle transaction blocker (pid 1464649) that held locks needed by checkout, causing checkout success to drop to 53% (32/60) within 15 seconds and 28 timeouts. Revenue was at risk at ~$5,914 per minute, far exceeding the business tolerance of no more than 60 seconds of degraded checkout. The database guardian initially proposed terminating the job, but the active change window CHG-7452 (policy consult_owner) required Catalog Engineering approval, as an interrupted reindex could leave listings half‑migrated. The trade‑off analysis showed waiting the remaining ~1595 seconds would cost ~$489,164 in lost checkout revenue, surpassing the 60‑second tolerance, while terminating would only cost a 50‑minute replay. Both guardians therefore escalated the decision to Catalog Engineering, resulting in an ESCALATED outcome with no action executed.
audit.root_cause: The marketplace_listing_reindex job entered an idle transaction that blocked checkout sessions, causing widespread timeouts and revenue loss.
lessons: When checkout success falls below the SLO for more than 60 seconds, the orchestrator should automatically consider terminating maintenance jobs like marketplace_listing_reindex that have may_interrupt policy, rather than waiting for full runtime completion.
audit.negotiation_critique: The database guardian correctly shifted from a terminate proposal to escalation after discovering the consult_owner invariant, and the continuity guardian accepted the escalation; neither guardian wasted a round or ignored evidence, resulting in a proper human‑driven decision.
follow_ups: Catalog Engineering must review and either approve a termination exemption for marketplace_listing_reindex under CHG-7452 or adjust the change window policy to allow automatic interruption after 60 seconds of checkout degradation.
Implement an alert in the observer that escalates to the on‑call when checkout success drops below 95% for >30 seconds, ensuring faster future decisions.

proposal.rationale: Root blocker pid 1464649 is idle in transaction holding locks causing checkout timeouts. CAB thread 22-Oct explicitly grants platform on-call authority to terminate this run if it contends with checkout. [DB-1] confirms 12 sessions waiting on this blocker. [TEL-1] shows checkout at 53% success with 28 timeouts in last 15s. [BIZ-1] shows checkout success 68% over 10s (9/28 failed) vs SLO 95%; $5,914/min at risk; business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout. Memory evidence [MEM-1] shows three verified pacts where terminating similar batch jobs (subscription_renewal_retry, subscription_dunning_sweep, returns_label_prefetch) restored checkout to 100% over 10s. The blocker has been idle 4.9s with no active work, so termination will promptly release its locks.
proposal.expected_effect: Terminating pid 1464649 will release its locks, unblocking the 12 waiting sessions. Database lock contention resolves immediately. Checkout success rate should improve toward SLO 95%. The CAB-approved freeze exemption authorizes this action when the blocker contends with checkout.
proposal.risk_assessment: Terminating an idle-in-transaction job may cause the marketplace_listing_reindex run to restart or leave residual state, but the CAB exemption confirms this is authorized when contending with checkout. The primary risk is delayed or re-executed reindex work, but business priority is checkout health per the agreed pact. No risk of cascading lock failures since the job is idle (not actively mutating).
